notes: §2002:12.2.6.2 SR24 confines a currency symbol to the usage of its WRITTEN literal-7's class. COBOL-2002 has no rule that implies a CURRENCY SIGN '$' clause (that is §2014:12.3.6.2 SR25), so the default '$' has no literal-7: FinalizeCurrencySigns joins CurrencyDefinition.DefaultDollar (IsDefaultSign) below DialectBehavior.ImpliedDollarCurrencyClause (VCR row 7.119, from 2014) and the analyzer asks no class of it. PIC $9.99 USAGE NATIONAL compiles at --std 2002 and edits $1.25; an explicit alphanumeric CURRENCY SIGN literal on a national item is still COBOL2883 at 2002; the implied '$' is still refused at 2014 and 2023 (PB5614).
